description: Host-supplied URLs whose scheme decides whether the value is a resource reference or an execution vector. The split that matters is navigation versus subresource: a `javascript:` URL in an `` runs the moment somebody clicks it, and the same string in an `` has been unable to run in any shipping engine for well over a decade. Every case below therefore states both.

fixtures.title: javascript: URL, unobfuscated
fixtures.rationale: In a navigation sink this is script execution in the page's own origin on activation, so nothing weaker than `rejected` is safe. In a subresource sink it is `inert`: the image loader has no script context, fetching `javascript:` is not defined, and the element fires `error`. `inert` here is a statement about the sink, not about the string — the same string one element over is the strongest case in this file.
fixtures.provenance: The canonical case in every public XSS suite (OWASP filter-evasion cheat sheet; cure53's DOMPurify URI tests).

fixtures.title: javascript: URL with mixed-case scheme
fixtures.rationale: URL schemes are ASCII case-insensitive (WHATWG URL §4.2). A policy that lowercases nothing before comparing rejects the plain case and admits this one, which is the single most common way a hand-rolled allowlist fails.
fixtures.provenance: WHATWG URL scheme-parsing rules; standard filter-evasion case.

fixtures.title: javascript: URL behind a leading C0 control character
fixtures.rationale: The URL parser strips leading C0 controls and spaces before it looks for a scheme, so the browser sees `javascript:` while a naive `startsWith('javascript:')` check sees something else entirely. The policy has to trim the same characters the parser does.
fixtures.provenance: WHATWG URL §4.4 'basic URL parser', leading/trailing C0-control-or-space removal.

fixtures.title: javascript: URL with a tab inside the scheme
fixtures.rationale: Tab, LF and CR are removed from anywhere in a URL by the parser, so this reaches the engine as `javascript:alert(1)`. A policy that compares the raw string sees a relative path with a tab in it.
fixtures.provenance: WHATWG URL §4.4, tab-and-newline removal; long-standing filter-evasion case.

fixtures.title: vbscript: URL
fixtures.rationale: No engine still in support executes it, but it belongs in the corpus because it is the case that shows whether a policy is an allowlist or a denylist: a denylist that names `javascript` and `data` admits this, and admits the next scheme nobody has thought of.

fixtures.title: data: URL carrying an HTML document
fixtures.rationale: Top-level navigation to `data:` has been blocked by engines since 2017, but a `data:text/html` URL is still live in a frame, in a `window.open`, and in any host that forwards the value somewhere else — the component must not be the thing that made it plausible. In an image sink the decoder refuses a `text/html` payload outright.
fixtures.provenance: Chrome 60 / Firefox 59 top-level data: navigation block; cure53 DOMPurify URI tests.

fixtures.title: data: URL carrying an SVG with an onload handler
fixtures.rationale: This is the case people get wrong in both directions. Inside `` it is genuinely inert — an image-loaded SVG has scripting disabled by specification. Inside `
fixtures.provenance: SVG 1.1 secure-static/animated processing modes; cure53 SVG sanitizer cases.

fixtures.title: file: URL pointing at a local path
fixtures.rationale: Not script execution — an information-disclosure and user-confusion case. A page cannot navigate to `file:` and an image cannot load it, so the practical harm is a link that looks like it does something and a URL bar that shows a local path. Included because an allowlist that admits it admits a scheme with no business in a web document.
fixtures.provenance: WHATWG URL special-scheme list; standard allowlist test.

fixtures.title: blob: URL minted by another origin
fixtures.rationale: A blob URL is only resolvable in the origin that created it, so this one resolves to nothing anywhere. It is here because `blob:` is the scheme a file-preview feature reaches for first, and the day a component starts calling `createObjectURL` its URL policy has to already have an opinion about which blob URLs it will render.
fixtures.provenance: File API blob URL store, origin-partitioned.
